items.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
items.summary_1line: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model on its own responses, guided by a fixed teacher. items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary_1line: Introduces CARE-OPD, a prefix-replay method for on-policy distillation of long-horizon agents that reports 59.5% task success on SWE-bench Verified while cutting training time by 45% versus asynchronous online OPD.
items.editor_note: Attacks rollout cost for long-horizon agents with prefix replay, with SWE-bench Verified numbers.

editorial.tldr: On Nov 8 an arXiv paper measured how much quantized or asynchronous rollout mismatch on-policy distillation (OPD) tolerates. Over Nov 9-10, three papers pushed OPD into agent training: recovering skills lost to best-checkpoint GRPO selection, picking teacher reference trajectories for multi-turn tool use, and training coding-agent file-memory habits.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 25: CARE-OPD, an arXiv paper, replays trajectory prefixes during on-policy distillation of long-horizon agents and reports 59.5% on SWE-bench Verified with 45% less training time than asynchronous online OPD.
editorial.why_it_matters: OPD is becoming a standard agent post-training step, and rollout generation is its dominant cost; CARE-OPD and the mismatch study both target that cost directly.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you distill long-horizon or coding agents on-policy, benchmark prefix replay against your async online OPD before buying more rollout compute; CARE-OPD's 45% saving is self-reported and unreplicated.

status.detail: A cluster of arXiv papers adapting OPD to agents and cutting its rollout cost; no independent replication yet.

beats.headline: Study tests how much training-inference mismatch OPD tolerates
beats.summary: Quantized inference and asynchronous rollouts cut OPD's generation cost but make student samples drift from the trained policy.

beats.headline: OPD moves into agent RL, tool-use trajectories, and coding-agent memory
beats.summary: Three papers in two days apply OPD to multi-turn agents rather than single-response students.

beats.headline: CARE-OPD claims 45% faster agent distillation via prefix replay

open_questions: What quantization level or rollout staleness does the mismatch study find safe for OPD students?
Does any group release code that reproduces Agentic-OPD's capability recovery on a different agent benchmark?
Does action-sequence alignment for choosing teacher references beat using any successful trajectory on a public tool-use benchmark?
Does CARE-OPD's 59.5% SWE-bench Verified result and 45% training-time cut hold when a third party reruns it?
Is prefix replay compatible with quantized rollouts, or do the two cost savings conflict?
